title: Kok Ming's feet
pageIntro: Try each piece of advice on the bench and see what happens to the fungi after 3 days. The options unlock when you have tried all four.
stem:
Kok Ming observed some fungi growing on his feet.

What is a good advice to reduce the growth of the fungi on his feet?
figure:
What each choice leaves for the fungi, and what happens after 3 days
ChoiceWarm?Dark?Damp?Food?After 3 days
No socks✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
Closed shoe✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
Open slipper✖ no✖ no✖ no✔ yesFungi hardly grow.
Keep the dead skin✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
hints: Fungi like four things: warmth, darkness, water and food. Which advice takes some of them away?
Look at your bench log. Which advice leaves the fungi with the fewest of the four things?
key: Good advice takes away at least one thing fungi like: warmth, darkness, water or food. A choice that changes none of them will not help.

options.text: Do not wear socks.
options.pick: Socks make feet hot and sweaty, so taking them off should help.
options.why: Without socks, the shoes still keep his feet warm, dark and damp, and the dead skin is still there. Nothing fungi like has been taken away.

options.text: Wear a closed shoe.
options.pick: A closed shoe covers the feet, so it seems to keep fungi away.
options.why: A closed shoe traps heat, keeps out light and holds in sweat. It gives fungi the warmth, darkness and water they like.

options.text: Wear an open slipper.
options.pick: Ask what fungi like: warm, dark, damp places with food. An open slipper lets in air and light, so the feet get cooler and drier.
options.why: Air and light reach the feet, so they are cooler, brighter and drier. Only the dead skin is left as food, so fungi grow much less.

options.text: Do not remove the dead skin on his feet.
options.pick: Dead skin is part of the foot, and leaving it alone seems harmless.
options.why: Fungi feed on dead skin. Leaving it gives them food. Removing it would take their food away.

title: Mei Ling's bread
pageIntro: Try each way of keeping bread on the bench and see how much mould grows after 3 days. The options unlock when you have tried all four.
stem:
Mei Ling found fuzzy green mould, which is a fungus, growing on a slice of bread that was left out for days. She wants the next loaf to stay mould-free.

Which is the best way to keep the bread?
figure:
What each choice leaves for the fungi, and what happens after 3 days
ChoiceWarm?Dark?Damp?Food?After 3 days
Sealed bag, warm cupboard✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
Beside a steaming kettle, bright kitchen✔ yes✖ no✔ yes✔ yesFungi keep growing.
Damp cloth, cupboard✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
Dry box, fridge✖ no✔ yes✖ no✔ yesFungi grow slowly.

tests.label: Beside a steaming kettle, bright kitchen

hints: Bread is food, so you cannot take that away. Which of the other three things can you change?
Compare how many of the four things each choice leaves. Which place leaves the fewest?
key: You cannot always take away the food. Keeping food cool and dry slows fungi down.

options.text: Seal the bread in a plastic bag and keep it in a warm cupboard.
options.pick: A sealed bag stops anything from getting onto the bread.
options.why: The bag traps moisture, and the cupboard is warm and dark. With the bread as food, fungi have all four things they like.

options.text: Leave the bread uncovered beside a steaming kettle in a bright kitchen.
options.pick: The kitchen is bright and uncovered bread can breathe, so mould should not grow.
options.why: Light helps a little, but the steam keeps the bread damp and the kettle keeps it warm. Fungi still have three of the four things.

options.text: Wrap the bread in a damp cloth and keep it in a cupboard.
options.pick: A damp cloth keeps the bread soft and fresh.
options.why: Water is one of the things fungi like. The damp cloth, the warm dark cupboard and the bread give fungi all four.

options.text: Keep the bread in a dry, covered box in the fridge.
options.pick: Ask which place is cool and dry. The fridge is cool, and a dry box keeps water away.
options.why: Cool and dry take away two of the four things. Fungi still have food and darkness, so they grow slowly.

title: Ali's wet shoes
pageIntro: Try each choice on the bench and see what happens to the fungi after 3 days. The options unlock when you have tried all four.
stem:
It rained heavily and Ali's school shoes were soaked. His mother wants to stop fungi growing inside them.

What should Ali do with the shoes?
figure:
What each choice leaves for the fungi, and what happens after 3 days
ChoiceWarm?Dark?Damp?Food?After 3 days
Open, in sun and air✔ yes✖ no✖ no✔ yesFungi grow slowly.
Dark shoe cabinet✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
Plastic bag✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
Wear them wet✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
hints: The inside of a shoe has dead skin and dirt, which are food. Which choice changes the other three things?
Does the choice leave the shoes wet, warm and dark?
key: You do not have to take away all four things. Taking away even two, such as water and darkness, slows fungi a lot.

options.text: Open the shoes and leave them in a sunny, airy place to dry.
options.pick: Take away what you can change easily: the water and the darkness.
options.why: Drying takes away water and light takes away darkness. Fungi still have warmth and food, so they grow slowly.

options.text: Put the wet shoes in the dark shoe cabinet straight away.
options.pick: Shoes belong in the cabinet, and a closed cabinet keeps them clean.
options.why: The cabinet is closed and dark, and the shoes stay wet. The dirt and dead skin inside are food. All four things are still there.

options.text: Put the wet shoes in a plastic bag.
options.pick: A bag stops the water from spreading to other things.
options.why: The bag traps the water and the warmth. The shoes stay damp and dark, so fungi keep growing.

options.text: Wear them again tomorrow while they are still wet.
options.pick: Body heat will dry them as he wears them.
options.why: His feet keep the shoes warm, and the shoes stay damp and dark. Nothing fungi like has been taken away.

title: Jia Hui's fungi hunt
source: Diagnostic question: where fungi grow best
pageIntro: Try each place on the bench and see how much fungi grow after 3 days. The options unlock when you have tried all four.
stem:
Jia Hui is looking for places where fungi grow well. This time the question is the other way round.

Where would fungi grow fastest?
figure:
What each choice leaves for the fungi, and what happens after 3 days
ChoiceWarm?Dark?Damp?Food?After 3 days
Bare rock, dry sunshine✔ yes✖ no✖ no✖ noFungi hardly grow.
Rotting log, damp forest✔ yes✔ yes✔ yes✔ yesFungi grow fast.
Clean plate, cold dry fridge✖ no✔ yes✖ no✖ noFungi hardly grow.
Dead leaves, dry sunshine✔ yes✖ no✖ no✔ yesFungi grow slowly.
hints: What do fungi feed on? Which places have dead things for food?
Which place has all four things: food, warmth, darkness and water?
key: To find where fungi grow fastest, look for food first. Then check for warmth, darkness and water.

options.text: On a bare rock in dry, bright sunshine.
options.pick: The sun makes the rock warm, and fungi like warmth.
options.why: Warmth is the only thing there. A rock is not food, and it is dry and bright.

options.text: On a rotting log in a damp, shaded forest.
options.pick: Look for a place with food, water, warmth and darkness.
options.why: A rotting log is dead plant matter, so it is food. It is also warm, damp and shaded. All four are there.

options.text: On a clean glass plate in a cold, dry fridge.
options.pick: A fridge is dark, and fungi like the dark.
options.why: Darkness is the only thing there. A clean plate has no food, and the fridge is cold and dry.

options.text: On a pile of dead leaves in dry, bright sunshine.
options.pick: Dead leaves are food and the sun keeps them warm.
options.why: There is food and warmth, but the leaves are dry and bright. Fungi would grow slowly at best.

title: Pei Shan's toes
stem:
Pei Shan found fungi growing between her toes.

Which advice would best reduce the growth of the fungi?
key: Take away what fungi like: dry the feet, remove the dead skin and let in air and light.

options.text: Wash her feet, dry them well and wear open sandals.
options.pick: Washing takes off dead skin, drying removes water, and sandals let in air and light.
options.why: Dead skin (food) is washed off, water is dried off, and air and light cool and brighten her feet. Fungi have much less of what they like.

options.text: Wear thick socks and closed shoes all day.
options.pick: Socks and shoes cover her feet and keep the fungi from spreading.
options.why: Socks and closed shoes keep her feet warm, dark and sweaty. That gives fungi what they like.

options.text: Soak her feet in warm water and leave them damp.
options.pick: Warm water kills fungi and keeps the skin clean.
options.why: Leaving her feet damp keeps the water that fungi need, and warmth helps them grow.

options.text: Leave the dead skin between her toes alone.
options.pick: Dead skin is part of the foot and does no harm.
options.why: Fungi feed on dead skin. If it stays, they keep their food.

title: Ahmad's belt
stem:
Ahmad found white mould growing on an old leather belt that he kept in a closed, dark drawer.

What should he do so that mould does not grow on the belt again?
key: Take away food (dirt), darkness and water. Put it where it is clean, dry and bright.

options.text: Put the belt back in the closed, dark drawer.
options.pick: The drawer keeps the belt safe from anything outside.
options.why: The drawer is dark and closed, so it stays warm and the belt can stay damp. Nothing fungi like is taken away.

options.text: Leave the dirt on it, because dirt does not matter.
options.pick: Dirt is only on the outside, so it cannot feed anything.
options.why: Fungi feed on dirt and other dead matter. Dirt left on the belt is food.

options.text: Spray air freshener on the belt.
options.pick: The smell hides the mould and seems to clean the belt.
options.why: Air freshener does not take away warmth, darkness, water or food. The fungi keep growing.

options.text: Wipe off the dirt and mould, then keep the belt in a dry, airy place.
options.pick: Wiping takes off the food, and a dry, airy place takes away water and darkness.
options.why: Removing dirt takes away food, and a dry airy place takes away water and darkness. Fungi have much less of what they like.

title: The fastest fungi
stem:
Four places are listed below.

In which place would fungi grow fastest?
key: Fungi grow fastest when all four things are there: food, warmth, darkness and water.

options.text: On a clean metal tray on a warm, dry, bright windowsill.
options.pick: The windowsill is warm, and fungi like warmth.
options.why: Warmth is the only thing there. A clean tray is not food, and the place is dry and bright.

options.text: In a dim corner of a bathroom floor, warm and damp, with hair and dead skin flakes.
options.pick: Hair and dead skin are food, and the corner is warm, dim and damp.
options.why: Food, warmth, darkness and water are all there, so fungi grow fast.

options.text: In a clean glass jar in a cold, dry fridge.
options.pick: The fridge is dark, and fungi like the dark.
options.why: Darkness is the only thing there. The jar has no food, and the fridge is cold and dry.

options.text: On old bread crusts on a dry, sunny windowsill.
options.pick: Bread crusts are food and the sun keeps them warm.
options.why: There is food and warmth, but it is dry and bright. Fungi would grow slowly.

title: Wei Jie's towel
stem:
Wei Jie's wet towel smells musty because fungi are growing on it.

What should he do to reduce the growth of the fungi?
key: Dry the towel and let in light. That takes away water and darkness.

options.text: Spray perfume on the towel.
options.pick: The perfume covers the smell and makes the towel fresh.
options.why: Perfume does not take away warmth, darkness, water or food. The fungi keep growing.

options.text: Fold the towel and keep it in a closed cupboard.
options.pick: Folding and closing the towel keeps it neat and away from dirt.
options.why: The towel stays wet, dark and warm in the cupboard, so fungi keep growing.

options.text: Hang the towel open in a sunny, breezy place.
options.pick: Hanging it open lets the water dry off and the light reach it.
options.why: Drying takes away water, and sunlight takes away darkness. Fungi grow much less.

options.text: Leave the towel on the damp bathroom floor.
options.pick: The towel is already wet, so it cannot get any worse.
options.why: The damp floor keeps the towel wet. Water is one of the things fungi like.

title: Most mould
stem:
Four setups are listed below.

Which setup would grow the most mould?
key: Look for food first. Then check for water, warmth and darkness. The best place has all four.

options.text: An old bread crust in a warm, damp cupboard.
options.pick: The crust is food, and the cupboard is warm, damp and dark.
options.why: All four things are there: food, warmth, darkness and water.

options.text: A clean spoon in a cold, dry fridge.
options.pick: A fridge is dark, and fungi like the dark.
options.why: Darkness is the only thing there. A clean spoon is not food, and the fridge is cold and dry.

options.text: A clean glass on a warm, dry, bright windowsill.
options.pick: The windowsill is warm, and fungi like warmth.
options.why: Warmth is the only thing there. A clean glass is not food, and the place is dry and bright.

options.text: An old bread crust on a dry, bright windowsill.
options.pick: The crust is food and the sun keeps it warm.
options.why: There is food and warmth, but it is dry and bright, so fungi grow slowly.
